conditions: Ideal linear spring, x measured from the unstretched length, with elastic potential energy zero at x=0.
spoken_aliases: u equals one half times k times x squared
elastic potential energy equals half the spring constant times the square of the extension

evidence: For the ideal spring force -kx, the potential derivative is kx. Integrating from equilibrium x=0 with U(0)=0 yields kx^2/2.
Reference checked 2026-11-27: https://openstax.org/books/university-physics-volume-1/pages/8-key-equations. Proposed maintainer approval, not independent human certification.
